headline: Refinance boom drives a swing back to profit
summary_short: UWM Holdings swung to $25.3M of net income attributable to UWMC ($0.09 basic/diluted EPS) in Q1 2026 versus a year-ago loss, as loan origination volume jumped 38.9% y/y to $44.9B on a refinancing surge; net cash used in operating activities widened to $(2,229.9)M as loan funding grew.
summary_long: Total revenue rose 47.0% y/y and 72.6% q/q to $901.4M as loan origination volume jumped 38.9% y/y to $44.9B (refinance volume more than doubled) on lower market rates, lifting gain margin to 1.23% from 0.94%. Consolidated net income was $170.4M versus a $247.0M loss a year ago; $25.3M was attributable to UWMC given its ~20% economic interest in Holdings LLC, producing $0.09 basic and diluted EPS versus a year-ago loss. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $160.9M from $57.8M. Cash fell to $424.0M as operating cash flow swung to $(2,229.9)M used, reflecting higher mortgage loans funded for sale; net financing and investing inflows of $1,626.2M and $524.3M partly offset the drain. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Refinance volume more than doubled to $26.3B from $10.6B on lower market rates and continued AI/tech investment in refinance market share, pushing total originations up 38.9% to $44.9B.
Loan production income rose 82.0% on the 38.9% origination-volume increase plus improved pricing; gain margin (production income / volume) rose to 1.23% from 0.94%.

Consolidated net income rose $417.4M on higher revenue and a far smaller MSR fair-value decline ($10.3M vs $388.6M); UWMC's own share reflects its ~20% economic interest in Holdings LLC, up from ~13% a year ago.
Tracks the swing in net income attributable to UWMC allocated under the two-class method between Class A and Class B common stock.

Diluted EPS assumes Class D units convert to Class A under the if-converted method, attributing all of Holdings LLC's net income to Class A shareholders, which is why the y/y comparison base differs from basic EPS.
Swing to $177.5M pretax income from a $260.8M loss mirrors the net income increase, ahead of a $7.1M tax provision versus a $13.8M benefit a year ago.

Cash flow statement shows the swing driven by a $1,058.4M increase in mortgage loans at fair value and a $702.8M increase in other assets, both tied to funding the higher origination volume ahead of loan sale.
$2,229.9M used in operating activities exceeded $1,626.2M of net financing inflows (mainly warehouse-line borrowings) and $524.3M of investing inflows, primarily MSR sale proceeds.
Roughly flat q/q; the y/y increase reflects the $1.0B of 2031 Senior Notes issued in September 2025, used to repay the matured $800.0M 2025 Senior Notes in November 2025.

y/y decline reflects $31.4M of Class A dividends and $129.1M of SFS Corp. distributions recorded in equity, plus non-controlling-interest re-measurement from Exchange Transactions, partly offset by net income.
